claims.statement: Scope is the ownership and isolation boundary: ScopeApplication creates Scopes idempotently by idempotency key and bootstraps a default Scope when none exists.

Capturing a Source persists evidence only and does not derive any Artifact; Sources.add stores a resolved Source without Artifact derivation, and the runtime capture path writes a content Source through the records or context journal.
Content Sources use caller-stable identity: a replay with the same source_id and content returns the existing Source, while conflicting content raises a SourceConflictError rather than overwriting.

Working Notes are explicit session-local Sources with optional expiry; they are never generation-eligible for ordinary Source-window processing and are only consumed by explicit consumers that resolve them through require_source_eligible.
Internal lineage-only Sources are ineligible for generation and are admitted only at their exact bound Artifact target revision.

Explicit Artifact Create and Replace commit a validated Revision directly without semantic generation; revise requires the same Artifact family and uses the caller-provided Artifact as the optimistic base.
Atomic Memory processes one Source window by preparing all decisions and then publishing once inside a transaction guarded by the source cursor generation, so a window is committed or not as a unit.
The Memory write gate can hold a pending Memory write with a structured reason and degrades to accept on backend failure, so an unavailable judge never blocks writes.

Experience incubation from eligible Sources never writes Artifacts directly: its plans and recurrence proposals are stored as Candidates through the review service in the same transaction that validates them.

Profile activation is policy-driven: an automatic policy commits generated Profile content as a Revision, while a review_required policy stores the same content as a pending Profile Candidate linked to the policy.

ReviewService keeps Candidate compare-and-swap and Artifact compare-and-swap inside one database transaction: approval publishes the reviewed Artifact and the Candidate result together, and overlapping approval retries return the stored result when the Candidate is already approved at the expected version.
Rejecting a Candidate requires a validated reason and the Candidate must be pending at the expected version; rejection is terminal and blocks later approval with a terminal-state error.

Server composition in create_server_app wires the lifespan, authentication middleware when configured, access control, request-id and resource-limit middleware, tracing and metrics, the MCP mount, and the dashboard when enabled.

The background artifact processing role cannot expose HTTP or MCP: create_server_app raises BackgroundRoleRequiresBackgroundRunnerError for role background, and the background role is served by a separate runner.

Settings enforce deployment boundaries: SQLite and embedded SeekDB accept only artifact_processing_role all, a non-loopback unauthenticated bind is rejected unless explicitly allowed, and an identity map or authentication requires enforced access mode.

Artifact processing runs one Supervisor per deployment or per dedicated Family group, holding a database lease with independent worker capacity per Family, and launches Workers as spawned child processes.

Background processing retries failed work with capped exponential backoff and jitter (delay = min(cap, base × 2^(failures−1) × jitter), with base 30 s and cap 1800 s by default). The set of processable Families is derived from processing_capabilities: an explicit artifact_processing_families declaration is used as-is; otherwise Dream-backed Families (skill, handoff, prompt) are declared only when Dream is enabled and the generation model's provider is a supported Dream provider.

The Python Client is an asynchronous facade over the public HTTP contract that refuses to send any request over plaintext non-loopback HTTP unless the caller explicitly opts in, and it closes only the HTTP client it created.
The CLI is a Typer shell assembled from installed roles: optional builtin and server command providers load only when their declared requirements are installed.
Host integrations are per-agent installers: installers() maps eleven agent names to installer classes, and select_hosts validates all requested targets before any write.
Session import is limited to the codex host, and capture helpers redact credential-like keys and truncate oversized events to a byte budget.

Ops accepts one bounded JSON request per process; its target binding and state directory come from the operator layer rather than the request, and rejected operations return fixed error codes so provider or path details are not echoed.
Ops configuration validation rejects a Unix-socket listener and any non-loopback host for managed service configuration.

The optional Rust Gateway admits every model request through a two-phase check: before_send must allow the admitted bytes before upstream egress, and before_release must allow the complete response before it reaches the client; the decisions remain in PowerContext Core.

Context admission is a read-only check over final model bytes: the check endpoint validates prepared-context bindings, with send validity of 60 seconds and response correlation of 300 seconds, and it never authorizes model spending.

During the Server lifespan a PluginManager is opened over the relational records database; plugin Workers are dispatched only when the supervisor mode is global and the artifact processing role is not api, while an api-role instance registers plugin families for reads only and never dispatches plugin Workers.
